title: fix(sim): credit an edge-break record only within its op's stated width
body:
**Stacked on #502** (chamfer/deburr edge breaks). Its commits show here until #502 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

The program sim forgave convicted columns down to a cached edge-break record's depth. The record is file data, so a hand-edited or corrupted project could state any depth and hide a real gouge under an inflated bevel (review note on #502). Each op's records are now held to the break width its own params state: `Chamfer2D` / `Deburr` `width`, against the record's `depth / slope`, with a micron of lattice slack. A wider record, or a record on a kind that declares no break, is dropped with a logged warning, and its columns are judged against the sharp model: stricter, never looser. The bound sits where the sim reads each op's records (`stock_sim::breaks::bounded`), so a fresh generation and a loaded file are judged alike.

## How tested

- New `edge_break_bound`, 3/3:
  - `an_inflated_record_no_longer_forgives_a_deeper_cut`: a chamfer ridden 0.3 mm deep, saved, its break depth hand-scaled ×5 in the file and reloaded. It still convicts.
  - `an_unedited_file_still_credits_its_own_break`
  - `the_bound_reads_the_ops_own_width`
- With the call site reverted, the first test fails ("the inflated record forgave a real gouge"). That is the bug.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 906 s: every crate suite is green, including #502's `edge_break_gate`, `deburr_links` and every stock_sim-mapped suite. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates. ui: only the three known GPU-adapter reds that are also red on main.

## Not exercised

A GUI view. The change only narrows what the verify credits.

Changelog: The gouge check credits a chamfer's or deburr's declared edge break only within the width the operation states, so a hand-edited project cannot widen it (#529)

Fixes #529

title: docs(process): the P? label pauses an issue until the maintainer sets a priority
body:
Adds the `P?` label (already created on GitHub): it pauses an issue until the maintainer sets a real priority.

- **AGENTS.md:** Pick's search excludes `label:"P?"`. A new rule: a `P?` issue is never picked, claimed, researched or re-prioritised by an agent, never sits beside a `P0`/`P1`/`P2`, and only the maintainer swaps it. Agents never file with `P?`.
- **README.md:** the Issues section explains `P?` for contributors.
- **review-prs skill, step 4:** a contributor's claim comment on a `P?` issue isn't mirrored; one reply says it's paused.

Docs and process only.

Changelog: none

title: feat(post): wire_edm and sinker_edm machine kinds and the .mch edm section
body:
## What changed

The first EDM sub-issue of #290 (design D1):
- **Machine kinds.** `Kind::WireEdm` / `Kind::SinkerEdm`, declared only (`wire_edm`, `sinker_edm`, plus synonyms such as `wedm` and `die-sinker`). No axis inventory infers an EDM. The required axes are X+Y for wire and Z for sinker. A blank EDM machine has no spindle or coolant.
- **`.mch` `edm` section** (`crates/post/src/machine/edm.rs`). Wire: lower and upper guide planes, max taper, wire diameters, AWT. Sinker: orbit patterns (CamCraft's geometry name plus the control's word), max orbit radius, pickup. Every key is optional and absent means not stated. Lengths scale with the file's unit. A garbled value refuses the file by name, and the same law is restated in `is_sane` for project files.
- **No current op family admits an EDM**, so every op is refused at the door on an EDM setup.
- **Post-time family gate (safety).** `op_streams` now re-checks every op's family against its own setup's machine and refuses by name. Before this, an op made on a mill still posted in a milling dialect after its setup was remounted onto a lathe or an EDM; the door only guarded creation.
- **No EDM post serves yet** (`post_serves` is false for both kinds).
- **Templates are test fixtures for now.** The empty wire/sinker templates live in `crates/app/tests/edm/` because every library machine must have a post. They join the library with #533 / #542.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the kinds and the section.

## How tested

- New `edm_machine`, 7/7: templates parse and declare their kinds; a filled section reads and inch-scales; nine garbled values each refuse by name; the kind words round-trip and unknown kinds still refuse; no milling op enters an EDM setup; **a milling op remounted onto an EDM is refused at post, and undo restores the post**; a project round-trips the section.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 913 s:
  - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion are green, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates.
  - app: green apart from `machine_library`, fixed by the follow-up commit that moved the templates to fixtures. The lathe, turning, mill-turn, drilling, c-axis, program-entry and conformance suites all ran, and the new gate's message appears in none of their logs, so it refused nothing outside its own test.
  - ui: only the five known reds that are also red on main.
- After the follow-up: `machine_library` 11/11, `machine` 32/32, `edm_machine` 7/7.

## Not exercised

- Any real EDM control. No EDM op or post exists yet; this is the schema seam only.
- The UI machine editor's kind picker still lists only mill, lathe and mill-turn (EDM setup pages are #535).

Changelog: Machine files can declare wire_edm and sinker_edm machines with an edm section; a program whose operation its setup's machine cannot run is refused at post (#530)

Fixes #530

title: fix(post): a trailing Go home entry merges with the end-of-program home
body:
## What changed
A Go home as the **last** entry was written twice: once as the entry, then again as the post's own end-of-program home before `M30` (found in the hands-on check of #469).

**Seam: each post's own script.** The posts differ, so an app-level drop would be wrong. Siemens' end-of-program home is `G53 Z0` only, Fanuc writes `G49` before a trip home under TCPM, and the lathe homes X then Z.
- **New PRELUDE helper:** `linesWritten()`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- **In each script:** the trip home records `homedAt`, and `onClose()` writes its own home only if a line was written since. In every post the trip home covers at least what the end-of-program home does.
- **Covered:** Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D and Fanuc Lathe. Heidenhain and Tormach already refuse a trip home by name.
- **Unchanged:** mid-program homes, Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes".
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/504-trailing-home.md`.

**Fanuc tail:**
```
before            after
G91 G28 Z0        G91 G28 Z0
G28 X0 Y0         G28 X0 Y0
G90               G90
G91 G28 Z0        M30
G28 X0 Y0
M30
```

## How tested
- **New tests (`program_entry`):**
  - `a_trailing_home_entry_merges_with_the_program_end_home` (Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D): one home for a trailing Go home; suppressed and skipped homes match the plain program; a mid-program home still gives two.
  - `the_lathe_post_writes_a_trailing_home_once`.
  - Both failed before the fix.
- **Goldens updated:** `program_entry/fanuc_pause_home.nc` and the Haas golden; each lost the duplicate home.
- **Gate:** the 31 app suites covering the posts (program_entry, posting, conformance, after_op, golden_cl, per_op_files, and the fanuc, lathe, tormach, inverted, coolant and probe post suites) and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised
A machine or simulator run. The change only removes a duplicate home at program end.

Changelog: A Go home as the last entry is written once: it merges with the post's end-of-program home (Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D, Fanuc Lathe) (#504)

Fixes #504

title: fix(ui): Fixtures page rows wrap inside the pane; place fields labelled
body:
**Stacked on #482** (#339 slice 4, fixture UX). It includes #482's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
The contributor's hands-on check of #482 found that the Fixtures page rows overflowed a normal-width properties pane. The position and Unmark/Delete were clipped, "Fixed (does not tu…" was truncated, and the place fields (three unlabelled boxes, shown only for the "draft" fixture) could not be found.

New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_rows.rs`:
- **Line 1:** the fixture name and its position (`x, y, z  yaw N°`), wrapped.
- **Line 2:** **Place…** (a toggle on every row), **Unmark** and **Delete**, left-aligned and wrapped.
- **Place form:** labelled **Place X / Place Y / Place Z / Place yaw** rows, then **Apply**.
- **Fixed checkbox:** the caption is the checkbox's own text, so it wraps; the old help text is its hover tooltip.
- **Import row:** wraps as well.

The commands are unchanged (`MoveFixture`, `SetFixtureFixed`, `UntagFixture`, `DeleteFixture`). Opening the place form is view state, not an undo step. `pages.rs` gets shorter.

## How tested
- **New:** `egui_app::tests::fixture_rows::fixture_rows_fit_the_default_pane_and_label_the_place_fields`. At 1280x720 with the default dock it checks that every row control and the four Place fields lie inside the pane, that the Fixed caption is not cut short, and that no command is queued. It failed before the fix.
- **Also passing:** ui `setup_tree`, `first_setup`, the fixture lib tests and `--test fixtures`, plus app `fixture_ux`. Clippy is clean. No snapshot PNG changed.
- **Known failure:** the headless-GPU test, which comes from this machine.

## Not exercised
A hands-on check. The headless render of the new layout was inspected (the place form is open, and every control is inside the pane).

Changelog: Fixtures page rows wrap inside the properties pane, and each fixture's Place… form has labelled X/Y/Z/yaw fields (#509)

Fixes #509

title: feat(app): recognise pockets and slots and turn them into operations
body:
## What changed

Pocket and slot recognition, headless (app layer and MCP; no GUI changes).

- **`camcraft_app::recognize`** (new module: `mod`, `walls`, `shape`, `op`):
  - `pockets_of(world, model)` reads the model's planar-face topology (`geometry::feature`, the same B-rep `list_features` and the pick tools use).
  - A level, up-facing face is a **floor** when the facets across its outer ring rise from it and lean into it (a concave edge), and those walls face each other across the floor.
  - Walled all round, it is a **closed pocket**. With wall-less spans it is an **open pocket**. A straight channel (at least 2 widths long, both long sides walled, each end wholly walled or wholly open, area within 3% of the shape) is a **slot**, with each end open, round or square.
  - Each result carries:
    - the outer ring (world XY, counter-clockwise), island count and area;
    - floor Z, top Z (highest wall point) and depth;
    - the **tightest inside corner radius** (0 = sharp, `None` where no two walls meet) and the **open spans**;
    - for a slot: centreline ends, **width**, length and end kinds.
  - Shoulders, corner steps, top faces and a plate around a boss are not pockets.
- **`recognize::operation_for`** maps a feature onto `CreateOperation`'s inputs, so creating it is one undoable History step with every field editable:
  - a pocket (or a slot with a square closed end, which a round cap would leave standing) becomes a **2D Pocket** on a pick of the floor face, with `bottom_z` at the selection bottom and `top_z` at the selection bottom + depth;
  - a slot with round or open ends becomes a **Slot** along its centreline: width, fixed heights, source stock, open ends running full width out to the floor's edge.
- **MCP `detect_pockets {model, create?, tool?, name?}`** lists the features, each with the floor's `face:0x…` id (the id `list_features` prints) and the operation kind it would create. With `create` it adds that operation, one undo step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/35-pocket-slot-recognition.md`.

Provenance: the concave-edge depression rule follows Joshi & Chang (CAD 20(2), 1988). The minimum-area rectangle follows Freeman & Shapira (CACM 18(7), 1975). No vendor material was consulted.

## How tested

Quick gate, debug: `pocket_recognition` 10/10, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_setup` 18/18, `cli` 2/2, `feature` 3/3. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Pinning tests, on watertight meshes built in code (`crates/app/tests/pocket_support`):
- `a_rectangular_pocket_is_closed_with_sharp_corners`
- `a_pocket_with_corner_radii_reports_its_tightest_corner` (r 4)
- `a_round_ended_closed_slot_is_a_slot_between_its_cap_centres`
- `a_through_slot_is_open_at_both_ends`
- `an_open_slot_with_a_square_end_machines_as_a_pocket`
- `parts_without_pockets_list_none` (plain block, shoulder, corner step, boss)
- `degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` (unknown model; NaN, infinite and zero-area facets; a torn half mesh)
- `a_recognised_pocket_becomes_an_undoable_pocket_that_cuts_to_its_floor`: generates with no Gouge, reaches the floor, stays inside the ring; undo removes it
- `an_open_slot_machined_as_a_pocket_cuts_its_floor_without_a_gouge`
- `a_recognised_slot_becomes_a_slot_cut_along_its_centreline`: checks the path geometry exactly; undo removes it
- MCP: `detect_pockets_lists_a_rounded_pocket_and_creates_its_pocket` (generate + verify ok; undo/redo), `detect_pockets_creates_a_slot_for_a_through_slot`, `detect_pockets_refuses_bad_arguments_by_name`

## Not exercised / known gaps

- **#510 (filed):** every typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is reported as a gouge today, recognised or not. The likely cause is the stadium region's chorded caps measured against `GOUGE_TOL`. Until #510 lands, a recognised slot's Slot op refuses to post. Its test checks the path geometry, not the verifier's verdict.
- **Not recognised:**
  - through pockets / windows (no floor face);
  - non-level floors and tilted setup frames (the read is world +Z);
  - curved slots, T-slots and undercuts.
  - Each level of a stepped pocket is its own feature.
- An open pocket's open side is not written into the area controls' open boundary. The tool's corner radius stays uncut where a wall meets an open edge.
- **GUI entry point:** #511. Not exercised on real STEP parts or by hand. The release-tier heavy lanes were not run.

Changelog: Pocket and slot recognition - `detect_pockets` (MCP) lists a model's closed/open pockets and slots (depth, corner radius, slot width, open sides) and creates the Pocket or Slot that machines one, one undo step (#35)

Fixes #35
